lectures.title: Institutions in news: health, science, space and environment

items: **ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research:** foundation stone laid on 12 October 2026 at Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh.
**Purpose of the centre:** research on high-altitude health, extreme weather, geographical isolation, climate variability and related illnesses.
**RMRC, Bhubaneswar:** developed the recombinant multi-stage malaria vaccine candidate **AdFalciVax**.
**ICMR–ICAR collaboration:** Mission SEHAT – Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation.
**Launch:** 11 May 2026 in New Delhi, jointly by Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda and Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
**What it does:** connects agricultural science, nutrition research and public-health policy.
**Objective:** “Healthy Food, Healthy Farms and a Healthy India”.

parts.t: National Health Authority and digital health platforms
items: Developed by NHA with support from IISc Bengaluru
Secure, governed analysis of health data under AB PM-JAY and ABDM
Developed by IIT Kanpur in collaboration with NHA
Redesigned as a citizen-facing digital health platform
Guidance for insurers, TPAs and other payers
Guidelines for digitally enabled hospitals and health institutions
**BODH – Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI:** a privacy-preserving benchmarking platform.
**BODH working:** allows evaluation of AI models on diverse, anonymised real-world health data; does not require sharing underlying datasets.
**National Resource Centre for EHR Standards (NRCeS):** associated with digital-health initiatives launched with NHA.
**National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX):** standardised exchange of health-claim information between hospitals and payers.

parts.t: BSL-4 laboratories: NIV Pune and GBRC Gandhinagar
items: **National Institute of Virology (NIV):** located in Pune, Maharashtra; India's only functional civilian BSL-4 laboratory at the time of publication.
**NIV in news:** mentioned in connection with India's high-containment laboratory infrastructure.
**BSL-4** is the highest biological containment level.
**GBRC BSL-4 Bio-Containment Facility:** foundation stone for the state-funded facility laid on 13 January 2026 by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
**Purpose:** research involving highly dangerous pathogens, including Ebola, Nipah and Marburg.

parts.t: Ayurveda, disease control and other health bodies
items: **All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA):** New Delhi; hosted **Saushrutam 2026** on 15 July 2026, held on Sushruta Jayanti.
**Saushrutam 2026:** inaugurated by President Droupadi Murmu; an AI-enabled 3 Tesla High-Field MRI facility was also inaugurated.
**National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM):** released a study on the professional careers of women Ayurveda graduates at Saushrutam 2026.
**NCISM role:** connected with the regulation and development of Indian systems of medicine.
**National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC):** dengue cases and deaths for 2023, 2024, 2025 and provisional 2026 figures are reproduced from its data.
**NIFTEM-K** (National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management – Kundli)
India's first dedicated Department of Military Medicine established here in Lucknow
Validated Bhutan's elimination of dog-transmitted human rabies; released Global TB Report 2025
Granted marketing authorisation for Qdenga in India
**IISc, Bengaluru:** supported NHA in developing the Secure Data Environment application, which provides secure analysis of health data generated under AB PM-JAY and ABDM.

**IISc in rankings and coverage:** mentioned in the Times Higher Education Asia University Rankings 2026; listed among India's prominent higher-education institutions in the Bharat Innovates 2026 coverage.
**IIT Kanpur:** developed BODH with the National Health Authority, a privacy-preserving platform for benchmarking Health AI.
**GeodCon-26:** organised by IIT Kanpur's National Centre for Geodesy from 11–13 March 2026; described as India's first national conference on geodesy.
**Inauguration:** remotely by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 8 August 2026 during IIT Delhi's 57th Convocation.
**Location and type:** installed at IIT Delhi's Sonipat campus, Haryana; an AI-oriented high-performance computing facility.
**Research applications:** large-scale AI models, material discovery, energy, healthcare and robotics.
**National Supercomputing Mission:** the DST Annual Report 2025–26 lists PARAM Pragya under it.
**Indian Institute of Astrophysics:** implementing agency for the COSMOS-2 Planetarium, to be constructed at Amaravati; connected with astronomy education and public outreach.
**IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre):** on 21 January 2026 formalised an agreement with a Pixxel-led consortium called **Allied Orbits**.
**The project:** India's first indigenous commercial Earth Observation satellite constellation, developed under the Earth Observation Public-Private Partnership (EO-PPP) programme.
**Consortium's task:** selected to design, build and operate the constellation.
**SpaDeX:** India became the fourth nation to achieve autonomous satellite docking.
**BlueBird Block-2:** launched by ISRO using LVM3 on 24 December 2025; placed in its intended low Earth orbit; the mission's payload weighed 6,100 kg.
**ISTRAC–SAMEER agreement:** ISRO's ISTRAC entered into an agreement with SAMEER for X-band deep-space communication amplifiers using indigenous GaN chips.
**Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC):** ISRO centre located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala; received a new Director in July 2026.
**VSSC Director:** Dr Upendra P. Rajeev assumed charge on 1 July 2026.
National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
**NCPOR:** based in Goa; implementing agency for India's proposed **Maitri II** research station in Antarctica, with a planned completion year of 2032.
**Existing Indian Antarctic stations:** Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri and Bharati.
**Antarctic research cooperation:** an agreement with the University of Canterbury, New Zealand, is mentioned.

parts.t: Telecom, semiconductors, DRDO and Survey of India
items: **Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT):** received the SKOCH Award 2025 on 19 January 2026, recognised for its Cell Broadcast Solution (CBS).
**3D Glass Solutions:** promoted the Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions project.
**India's first advanced 3D chip packaging unit:** foundation stone laid at Info Valley, Bhubaneswar.
**Nature of the unit:** an advanced packaging and embedded glass-substrate ATMP facility, not a conventional semiconductor fabrication plant.
**Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket:** DRDO conducted a successful flight test on 8 July 2026 at Integrated Test Range, Chandipur.
**SSPL:** developed indigenous processes for manufacturing 4-inch Silicon Carbide wafers.
**GAETEC, Hyderabad:** mentioned in connection with limited production capability for indigenous GaN-on-SiC MMICs.

**Arunachal Pradesh place names:** on 7 August 2026 the Government of India, in consultation with Arunachal Pradesh, identified 27 places/features in the State by standard place and feature names on official Survey of India maps.
**Wildlife Institute of India (WII):** described as a premier wildlife research institute.
**Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict:** national-level centre established at WII–SACON, Coimbatore; inaugurated on 10 July 2026 by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav.
**Also launched:** the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal.
**Released:** the first edition of *Current Status of Human–Wildlife Conflict in India: An Overview*.
**Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON):** Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu; associated with WII; hosts the Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict.
**Aim of the centre:** to strengthen research and response to human–wildlife conflict.
**Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE):** Kochi, Kerala; associated with the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
**Bhavasagara Referral Centre:** designated as the National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna; holds more than 3,560 taxonomically identified, geo-referenced voucher specimens.
**Natural History Museum, Mizoram University:** at Aizawl, Mizoram; designated India's 21st Designated Repository under Section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
**Purpose of the designation:** related to the conservation and preservation of biological specimens.
**Geological Survey of India (GSI):** Varsha Ashok Aglawe was appointed as the 54th Director General, the first woman to hold the position; GSI is also mentioned in the appointments section.
**ICAR–FCI MoU:** ICAR and the Food Corporation of India signed an MoU on 30 September 2026.
**Objective:** research on alternative fumigation technologies for safe and sustainable food-commodity storage.
**ICAR-CIPHET (Central Institute of Post-Harvest Engineering and Technology):** Ludhiana, Punjab; implementing institution for the ICAR–FCI research programme.
**Programme design:** planned in two phases; the first phase has an approved outlay of ₹3.28 crore for two years.
**National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE):** estimated approximately 102.18 GWp of floating-solar potential across reservoirs and suitable inland water bodies.
**Context of the estimate:** mentioned in connection with the PM-SSY floating-solar scheme.
**NSTI Hyderabad:** a renewable-energy skilling Centre of Excellence was proposed here in the India–Germany cooperation section.
**NSTI Bhubaneswar:** a mining Centre of Excellence was proposed here in the India–Australia cooperation section.

Nine Buddhist caves beside the Baghni River in Madhya Pradesh.
Complex of 20 caves, developed mainly during the late 4th and early 5th centuries under Gupta patronage.
Bateshwar, Padavali and Kakanmath in Morena; illustrate Nagara architecture under Gurjara-Pratihara and Kachchhapaghata patronage.
Fortified capital of the Raj Gond; located in Sehore district, Madhya Pradesh.

India's World Heritage profile and Sarnath
items: **Recent Indian additions:** Sarnath (2026), Maratha Military Landscapes (2025), Moidams (2024).
**Sarnath:** Buddhist site included in UNESCO's World Heritage List on 25 July 2026; located in Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh.
With **Sarnath**, India's World Heritage Sites total became **45**.
**World Heritage Convention, 1972:** protects cultural and natural heritage possessing Outstanding Universal Value (OUV).
**Common heritage:** such heritage is treated as the common heritage of humanity.

parts.t: Health missions: SEHAT, ABDM and JANANI
items: **Mission SEHAT (health and agriculture):** its central idea is to connect agricultural progress with nutrition and measurable public-health outcomes through ICAR and ICMR.
**Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM):** more than 90 crore Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHAs) created by 30 May 2026; nearly half of ABHA holders were women.
**ABDM milestone:** the mission's fifth anniversary in September 2026; it is connected with digital health platforms and interoperable health records.
**Full form:** Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care.
**Launch:** by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare at the 10th National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity in Chandigarh.
**Design:** to strengthen maternal and child healthcare through digital tracking, interoperable health records and real-time monitoring.
**Core features:** upgraded version of the existing Reproductive and Child Health portal; creates longitudinal health records.
**Covers:** antenatal care, delivery preparedness, delivery, postnatal care, newborn care, home-based newborn and young-child care, and family planning.
**Cards and links:** QR-enabled digital Mother and Child Health cards; can integrate with U-WIN and POSHAN platforms.

parts.t: Health AI and aid: SAHI, BODH, Aarogya Setu 2.0, BHISHM
items: **SAHI – Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India:** launched on 17 February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit 2026.
**What SAHI is:** a national guidance framework for responsible adoption of AI across India's healthcare system.
**SAHI focus areas:** governance, data stewardship, validation, deployment and monitoring of AI tools.
**SAHI aim:** to coordinate healthcare institutions, technology developers, researchers and policymakers.
**BODH – Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI:** launched along with SAHI on 17 February 2026; developed by IIT Kanpur in collaboration with the National Health Authority.
**BODH design:** privacy-preserving benchmarking platform for Health AI, to support safe, ethical, evidence-based, transparent and inclusive AI use in healthcare.
**Aarogya Setu 2.0:** launched on 29 June 2026 by Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi; redesigned as a citizen-facing digital health platform.
BHISHM – Bharat Health Initiative for Sahyog, Hita and Maitri
**What it is:** portable, indigenously developed medical units; rapidly deployable modular hospitals.
**Use:** support emergency surgery, trauma care and disaster response; part of India's Aarogya Maitri Initiative.
**Deployment:** during Operation Amistad for Venezuela in June 2026.
**Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander hop experiment:** ISRO shared findings on 18 May 2026.
**The hop:** Vikram lander reignited its engines, performed a controlled hop and landed approximately 50 cm from its original position.
**Purpose:** test ascent capabilities relevant to future lunar sample-return missions.
**ChaSTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment):** a lunar thermometer; re-penetrated the lunar regolith at the new landing location.
**Soil findings:** a two-layer structure was identified in the upper 6.5 cm; soil cohesion and density increased with depth.
**Temperature finding:** local craters and depressions caused temperatures to decline faster than global models predicted.
**Effect of engine firing:** removed the upper 3 cm of regolith and slightly compacted the material underneath.
**Chandrayaan-5 – LUPEX:** official name Lunar Polar Exploration (LUPEX) Mission; a joint India–Japan lunar exploration mission.
**Launch site:** ISRO began assessing a launch site in Japan for the joint mission (report dated 28 April 2026).
**Aditya-L1:** studies the Sun–Earth system from the vicinity of the L1 Lagrange point.
**Fourth cycle:** ISRO announced the fourth Announcement of Opportunity cycle for solar observations on 16 October 2026.
**Data:** more than 37 TB of scientific data had been made public by October 2026.
**Gaganyaan:** on 16 October 2026 ISRO completed separation tests of the Crew Module and Service Module.
**Test centre:** the test activity was associated with the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Thiruvananthapuram.
**SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment):** India became the fourth nation to achieve autonomous satellite docking; an important Indian space milestone.

parts.t: Artemis II and Japan's MMX mission
items: **Artemis II:** NASA's Artemis II lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on 1 April 2026; sent the first humans towards the Moon since 1972; the crew completed a lunar flyby.
**Significance:** returned humans to the vicinity of the Moon for the first time in 53 years after the final Apollo lunar mission.
**Apollo 17 (1972):** humans landed on the Moon. **Artemis II (2026):** humans travelled towards and around the Moon; it was not a lunar landing.
**Agency and launch:** Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA); launched on 20 October 2026 by H3 Flight No. 10 from Tanegashima Space Center, Japan.
**Objective:** achieve the world's first sample return from the Martian system; planned mission duration approximately five years.
**Mission objectives:** study Phobos and Deimos, the two moons of Mars; return at least 10 grams of material from Phobos.

**Science questions:** determine whether the moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars; improve understanding of planetary formation and the delivery of water and organic compounds.
**Technical features:** three spacecraft modules (propulsion, exploration, return); solar panels for electricity and chemical propulsion for manoeuvres.
**Orbit and payload:** quasi-satellite orbit around Mars near Phobos; carries 13 mission instruments.
Measures surface distance using laser pulses
Measures gamma rays and neutrons to determine elemental composition

parts.t: LVM3-M6 BlueBird Block-2 and Mission Aagaman
items: **LVM3-M6:** launched on 24 December 2025; launch vehicle LVM3; satellite BlueBird Block-2; customer AST SpaceMobile, USA; placed in Low Earth Orbit.
**Records:** heaviest payload launched by LVM3 from Indian soil; BlueBird Block-2 is described as the largest commercial communications satellite deployed into LEO.
**Constellation:** the global LEO constellation is designed to provide direct-to-mobile connectivity, including 4G/5G voice, video calls, text messages, streaming and data services.
**Mission Aagaman:** associated with India's first privately developed orbital launch vehicle, **Vikram-1**; successful flight mentioned on 18 July 2026.
**Developer and site:** Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace; launch location Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

parts.t: Private space: MOI-1A, Pathfinder and the EO constellation
items: **MOI-1A (orbital computing satellite):** developed by TakeMe2Space; announced on 2 October 2026; India's first indigenous orbital computing satellite.
**MOI-1A application:** artificial-intelligence-based data processing in space itself.
**Pathfinder (orbital data-centre satellite):** announced on 4 May 2026; a collaboration between Pixxel and Sarvam; described as India's first orbital data-centre satellite.
**Pixxel's role:** design, build, launch and operate the satellite; hyperspectral imaging.
**Sarvam AI's role:** AI backbone, GPUs, models and inference capabilities.
India's first private Earth Observation satellite constellation
**Agreement:** IN-SPACe formalised an agreement on 21 January 2026 with the Pixxel-led consortium called Allied Orbits.
**Programme and objective:** Earth Observation Public-Private Partnership (EO-PPP); to establish India's first indigenous commercial Earth Observation satellite constellation.
**Consortium:** Pixxel Space India, Piersight Space, SatSure Analytics India and Dhruva Space.
**Sensors:** panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and microwave Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR).
**Applications:** agriculture, infrastructure planning, climate monitoring, disaster response, agricultural credit, water management and policy planning.

parts.t: Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and the original mission
items: **Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0:** approved on 10 March 2026 by the Union Cabinet under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
**Objective:** transform Jal Jeevan Mission from an infrastructure-creation programme into a service-based model.
**Sujalam Bharat:** an integrated national digital platform, developed by March 2026.
**Coverage:** total rural households 19.36 crore; households with tap-water access as of March 2026 approximately 15.80 crore (81.61%).
**Target:** tap-water connections to all 19.36 crore rural households by December 2028; all Gram Panchayats are to receive Har Ghar Jal certification.
**Service model:** shift towards a utility-based service-delivery model, intended to ensure 24×7 rural drinking-water supply; linked to the goal of Viksit Bharat @2047.
Tap-water supply to every rural household by 2024
**Rural households with tap connections at launch**

parts.t: Export Promotion, Digital Agriculture and IndiaAI missions
items: **Export Promotion Mission:** approved in November 2025; duration FY 2025–26 to FY 2030–31; total outlay ₹25,060 crore.
**Interventions and focus:** two initial interventions launched under the Niryat Protsahan sub-scheme; focus on strengthening exports of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
**Farmer ID:** implemented under the Digital Agriculture Mission; provides a unique digital identity to farmers.
**Farmer ID enables easier access to:** government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief.
**Progress:** 11 crore Farmer IDs had been created by 23 October 2026; deadline mentioned: 31 March 2027.
**IndiaAI Mission:** approved by the Government of India in March 2024.
**AIKosh:** a key pillar of the IndiaAI Mission; functions as India's unified data platform.
**AIKosh users:** supports researchers, startups, developers and students; facilitates development of AI-based solutions using trusted national resources.
**India Semiconductor Mission:** two additional semiconductor projects were approved on 5 May 2026; both are to be established in Gujarat.
**Project 1:** India's first commercial Mini/Micro-LED display facility based on Gallium Nitride technology.
**Project 2:** semiconductor packaging, assembly and testing facilities, including discrete semiconductors.
**India Semiconductor Mission 2.0:** announced in Union Budget 2026–27.
**ISM 2.0 focus areas:** semiconductor equipment and materials; full-stack intellectual property; supply-chain strengthening; industry-led research and development; training and capacity building.
